newsitem.title: USA: FPL Group posts higher profits after hot summer.
newsitem.headline: FPL Group posts higher profits after hot summer.

text.p: FPL Group Inc. said Tuesday that a long, hot summer that kept its customers air conditioners purring helped push its profits up 4 percent in the third quarter.

FPL, which owns Florida Power & Light Co., one of the largest electric utilities in the nation, said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 grew to $250 million, or $1.44 a share, from $240 million, or $1.37 per share.
The company, based in Juno Beach, Fla., said its revenues rose to $1.77 billion from $1.58 billion.

"The favourable results for the quarter reflect very warm weather this summer as well as continuing growth in our customer base and lower operating expenses," Michael Yackira, FPL vice president and chief financial officer, said in a statement.
For the first nine months of the year FPL Group said its net income grew to $494 million, or $2.84 a share, from $479 million, or $2.73 per share.
Revenues for the nine months expanded to $4.60 billion from $4.23 billion.
FPL Group's stock added 12.5 cents to $43.875 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
